Terminate two Cat5e cables to keystone jacks — 9 steps.
You will need: 110-style punch-down tool (a small hand tool that pushes wire into a plastic slot and trims the end at the same time), Keystone jack x2 (small snap-in network socket, T568B wiring, to match the color chart printed on its body), Small flathead screwdriver, Wire stripper or sharp scissors, Short Cat5e patch cord (a ready-made cable with plugs on both ends, any length 0.5–2 ft), Cable tester (a two-piece device: plug one end of the finished link into the master unit, the other end into the remote unit, and watch the numbered LEDs flash in sequence 1–8)

Step 1 of 9: Identify the two blue Cat5e cables
Trace each of the two blue Cat5e cables (the round, solid-blue jacket cables) from where they enter the panel to the point where they are currently punched into the old telephone distribution block (the strip of colored plastic terminals in the center of the panel). Note which port each cable occupies so you can re-use the same cable later.
Do not touch: coax splitter and coax cables · yellow-green ground wire · black cables
Stop if: If either cable feels warm, smells burnt, or shows any melted jacket, stop and contact a licensed low-voltage technician.
Next photo must show: Photo showing both blue Cat5e cables clearly traced to their current punch-down positions on the old block, with nothing else disturbed.
